scope: Feature branch 009-asking-to-agree vs origin/main (`git diff origin/main...HEAD`, reviewed at 34a1d70; code head 85c7776). One reviewer, three lenses in one pass: correctness, spec-compliance, security. Subject: mvp_compliance/ (views.py, models.py, urls.py, templates, script), tests/, docs/, README.md, CHANGELOG.md, CONTEXT.md, demo/. specs/ read as input only. Evidence gathered: full suite run (578 passed); 73 read-only probes run from /tmp against the branch (50 `next` values, 11 `agree` values, races, docs examples); 20 mutations of views.py/models.py/urls.py/outstanding.html applied to a scratch copy in /tmp, every one killed by a named test (no atomic, no own-address check, decide from the submission, no csrf_protect, no ignore_conflicts, no redirect when nothing outstanding, toggles not kept, changed always False, no log, address never read, no order_by, honour any published version, no published check, no sign-in, extra allowed host, RecordError not caught, wording on the page, link without ?version=, slug not reserved, route after the slug route). Nothing in the repository was edited. TESTS SWEPT: 70 (69 added test functions: 58 in tests/test_views.py, 10 in tests/test_models.py incl. the new reserved-slug test, 1 in tests/test_admin.py; plus the 1 edited parametrize of D24 and the edited PAGE_TEMPLATES list of T001). No same-expression assertion, no status code the failing case shares, no query bound measured with one row (1 vs 10 at tests/test_views.py query-count tests, 1 vs 5 at tests/test_models.py:1470), no skip/early return found. Two gaps are TEST-001 and TEST-002. ORCHESTRATOR QUESTIONS. (1) `next` / get_destination() / is_own_address() (mvp_compliance/views.py:266-302). Leaves the site: none found. 50 values probed, including https://, //host, ///host, /\host, /<TAB>/host, javascript:, ftp://, http:x, http:///x, //[::1, NUL-prefixed, CR/LF, 5000 chars: every off-site form came back as the default. An https address on the same host is followed from an http request (on-site, intended). Raises: none; CR/LF is percent-encoded into Location by HttpResponseRedirect, `http://[` and `/a//[b` do not raise in urljoin. Loops: no unbounded loop from `next`, because a redirect to the page drops `next` and the next GET falls to the default. Values that reach the page for one extra hop are in SEC-001 (`/legal/agree/%2e`). The one real loop is operator-made: MVP_COMPLIANCE_AGREEMENT_REDIRECT_URL = 'mvp_compliance:agree' answers 302 -> /legal/agree/ forever for a person with nothing outstanding (probed); docs/pages.md:266 says the setting is followed as written, so it is recorded here and not as a finding. A setting naming a URL that does not reverse raises NoReverseMatch on every draw of the page (views.py:284, called from get_context_data at :381), also operator-made. (2) `agree` and `listed` (views.py:336-344). `agreed` is built only from self.entries, the versions in force of documents outstanding for request.user read at :338, filtered by string membership; no value is parsed, so no value raises (probed: '', NUL, '1e3', 400 digits, ' 1', '01', '+1', Arabic digit, 'True': all 200, nothing recorded). A superseded version, a draft, an already-accepted version and a notice's version record nothing (tests/test_views.py test_a_submission_naming_a_version_that_was_not_listed_records_nothing; mutation M13 killed). `listed` gates nothing: agree=<pk> with listed=[] records the version in force and redirects (probed, 302, 1 acceptance). That is the version the page would list for that user at that moment, sent by the signed-in user under CSRF, and `listed` is client-supplied, so it could not be a control; FR-005 holds for every submission a rendered page can produce. The one way a version not in force gets recorded is the read/write race in COR-001. (3) CSRF and sign-in. csrf_protect on dispatch at views.py:198, LoginRequiredMixin at :199. No token -> 403 and nothing recorded, with and without CsrfViewMiddleware (tests + mutation M4 killed). The CSRF check runs before the sign-in check, so an anonymous POST without a token is 403, not a redirect. A POST after the session ended, with the CSRF cookie still held, is 302 to /account/login/?next=/legal/agree/%3Fnext%3D... and records nothing (probed), so the destination survives through the form's action URL (agreement.html:31 has no action). PUT/PATCH/DELETE are 405. (4) Failure path (views.py:345-353). Logs one ERROR record on mvp_compliance.views with the traceback and request.user.pk only: no request body, no address, no token. Renders get_context_data(failed=True): the fixed sentence at agreement.html:12, the toggles that were on, nothing of the exception (test asserts the cause text is absent; M10 and M17 killed). The write sits in transaction.atomic() at :347 (M1 killed). Any other exception type from a project's record_agreed() is a 500, as docs/pages.md says. (5) No `listed` posted: `listed` is empty, so `changed` at views.py:339 is True whenever anything is outstanding before the write. A person who left something required sees `changed` (in the package's template the 'A document changed while you were reading' alert) in place of `missing`; when everything was agreed they are redirected as normal, and a failed write still draws `failed`. Probed: {'missing': False, 'changed': True} for both a partial and an empty submission. This is stated at docs/pages.md:412-414, so it is documented behaviour; it is untested (TEST-002). (6) record_many() against record() (mvp_compliance/models.py:923-971), claim by claim. Already accepted is passed over and its record untouched: true, unique constraint one_acceptance_per_person_per_version + ignore_conflicts (:969), tested, M5 killed. One refused version means nothing written: true for a draft (check at :945 precedes the single write) and for a notice (AcceptanceQuerySet.bulk_create at :773 refuses before super()). Unsaved user raises RecordError: true (subject_of at :958; probed, raises even for an empty batch), untested (TEST-001). Address read only when the setting is on and only REMOTE_ADDR: true (:950-956). No save signals: true, bulk_create. Needs ignore-conflicts support: true. docs/models.md 'one query to look for a notice and one to write, whether the batch holds one version or fifty': probed with fifty, 2 queries. Duplicates in the batch and a generator argument both work (probed). Differences the docs do not hide: returns None (stated), one accepted_at for the batch (stated). A superseded version is accepted by both record() and record_many(), as before. (7) See TESTS SWEPT above: 70. (8) Docs examples run against the branch. docs/models.md: record_many(user, [privacy.current, terms.current], request=request) runs (Document.current is a property, models.py:221); record_many(user, versions, request=request) runs. docs/pages.md: the link example resolves; the replacement template example was rendered and submitted as written (200, two `listed`, two `agree`, CSRF token, then 302 to the destination); `{% block page.content %}` exists in page_view.html; the LOGGING example is valid dictConfig; the three settings values resolve; the ProjectAgreementView example matches record_agreed(self, versions) (AuditEntry and the urls imports are the reader's own). The checkout example raises for a visitor who is not signed in: DOC-001. Documented value sets checked member by member: the template context table (entries/document/version/optional/field, required_count, destination, redirect_field_name, failed, missing, changed) against views.py:361-383 and :353-359; entry.field keys (name, value, id, aria-describedby, data-required, checked) against :367-378; the own-address forms listed at docs/pages.md:248-252 against the parametrised test; RESERVED_SLUGS. All match. Constitution pass: every string the diff adds to views and templates is wrapped and present in locale/en django.po; no model field added, makemigrations --check clean; no leading-underscore name, compatibility alias or {% include %} introduced; no multi-line {# #} in the two new templates.

findings.claim: The view example under 'Sending a person to the page' raises RecordError (a 500) for any visitor who is not signed in.
findings.evidence: docs/pages.md:230-234 defines `def checkout(request)` with no sign-in guard and calls `Document.objects.outstanding_for(request.user).exists()`. DocumentQuerySet.outstanding_for (mvp_compliance/models.py:108) calls Acceptance.subject_of(user), which raises RecordError when user.pk is None (models.py:1073-1079). AnonymousUser.pk is None. Probed on the branch: `Document.objects.outstanding_for(AnonymousUser()).exists()` -> `RecordError: Cannot record an acceptance or a publisher for a user with no primary key.` The page itself sends such a visitor to sign in; the example that leads to it does not get that far. It is the only code example of the feature's one integration route (US-4, FR-026).
findings.reproduction: Copy the example into a project, request the view without signing in: RecordError propagates, 500. Or in a shell: `from django.contrib.auth.models import AnonymousUser; Document.objects.outstanding_for(AnonymousUser()).exists()`.
findings.suggested_fix: In the example only: import `login_required` from django.contrib.auth.decorators and decorate `checkout` with it. No code change. Verify by reading the example: the call to outstanding_for() must be unreachable for request.user.is_authenticated == False.

findings.claim: The versions to record are chosen by one read and written later, so a change between the two is not passed over: a version replaced in that window is still recorded, and a document made a notice in that window fails the whole submission.
findings.evidence: mvp_compliance/views.py:338 reads the entries, :348 writes them. record_many() accepts any published version, superseded included (models.py:945). Probed by publishing a new version inside record_agreed before the write: response 200 with missing=True (not changed), and an acceptance of the replaced version exists; FR-005 says a version is recorded 'only while that version is still the current version', and docs/pages.md says 'Only the version in force of a document outstanding for that person is recorded'. Probed by making one of two agreed documents a notice in the same window: refuse_if_notice raises RecordError, the page is drawn with failed=True, an error is logged and the other agreement is not kept; FR-013 says such a document is passed over without failing the submission. The person is never let through wrongly in either case (ADR 0021 holds). The window is a few milliseconds and needs an editor publishing at that instant, hence low.
findings.reproduction: Patch AgreementView.record_agreed to publish a new version of the agreed document (or set the document's kind to notice) and then call the original; POST agree=<old pk>.
findings.suggested_fix: Smallest honest remedy is a sentence, not a mechanism: say in docs/pages.md ('When the list changed while it was open') and ADR 0021 that a change landing between the page's read and its write can leave an acceptance of the version just replaced, or draw the submission as failed, and that the person is asked again either way. Closing the window would need row locks on the documents, which this consequence does not justify.

findings.claim: is_own_address() resolves dot segments before it percent-decodes, so the page's own address written with an encoded dot is followed as a destination.
findings.evidence: mvp_compliance/views.py:301 `unquote(urlsplit(urljoin(own, destination)).path)`: urljoin removes `.`/`..` segments, then unquote turns `%2e` into `.` with nothing resolving it. Probed: next=/legal/agree/%2e -> context destination '/legal/agree/%2e' and Location '/legal/agree/%2e' (also /legal/x/%2e%2e/agree/ by the same path). Browsers treat %2e as a dot segment (WHATWG URL), so the person lands on /legal/agree/ again; FR-016 and docs/pages.md:248-252 say the page's own address, 'with a letter percent-encoded', is replaced by the default. Consequence is one extra redirect, never a loop and never off-site: the second request carries no `next` and falls to the default. Browser behaviour was not run here, hence likely.
findings.reproduction: Signed in with one outstanding document: POST agree=<pk>&next=/legal/agree/%2e and read Location.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve after decoding: `path = urlsplit(urljoin(own, unquote(urlsplit(urljoin(own, destination)).path))).path`, or the equivalent one more urljoin over the unquoted path. Add '/legal/agree/%2e' and '/legal/x/%2e%2e/agree/' to the parametrised test_the_pages_own_address_is_replaced_by_the_default; the repaired test must fail when that second resolution is removed.

findings.claim: record_many() documents that it raises RecordError for a user that has not been saved, and no test would notice if it stopped.
findings.evidence: Docstring at mvp_compliance/models.py:941-942. TestRecordMany (tests/test_models.py:1386-1478) has no case with an unsaved user; record() has one at tests/test_models.py:1246. The behaviour is there today (probed: record_many(unsaved_user, []) raises RecordError via subject_of at models.py:958).
findings.suggested_fix: One test in TestRecordMany: record_many(get_user_model()(username='not-saved'), [published_version]) raises RecordError and Acceptance.objects.exists() is False. It must fail when `subject = Acceptance.subject_of(user)` is replaced by `subject = str(user.pk)`.

findings.claim: The documented behaviour of a submission that carries no `listed` values is asserted by no test.
findings.evidence: docs/pages.md:412-414 tells a project replacing the template that 'a submission without it is always drawn as `changed`'. Every submission helper in tests/test_views.py sends `listed`, and the one test that sends a different list still sends one. The behaviour holds today (probed: missing False, changed True). Replacing views.py:339 with `changed = bool(listed) and any(...)` was not run as a mutation, but no test posts without `listed`, so nothing can go red.
findings.suggested_fix: One test: two outstanding documents, POST agree=<first pk> and `next` with no `listed`; assert context['changed'] is true and 'missing' is not. It must fail under `changed = bool(listed) and any(...)`.

findings.claim: Five lines added by this diff run past 88 characters.
findings.evidence: mvp_compliance/views.py:362 (docstring of get_context_data); mvp_compliance/models.py:948 (the message string in record_many, a copy of the one in record()); demo/management/commands/seed_demo.py:437 (docstring of make_asked); tests/test_views.py:1835 (docstring of the `optional` fixture); tests/test_views.py:2147 (the def line of test_a_person_with_nothing_outstanding_and_a_foreign_destination_gets_the_default). ruff check passes, so the linter does not enforce the limit on these; the brief names it as a standard.
findings.suggested_fix: Shorten the three docstrings and the test name. For models.py:948 see COR-002, which removes the copied line.

findings.claim: record_many() repeats record()'s refusal of an unpublished version and its reading of the connecting address line for line, so the two routes can drift apart on exactly the guarantees the docs say they share.
findings.evidence: mvp_compliance/models.py:895-900 and :945-950 (same check, same message); :904-911 and :951-957 (same setting read, same REMOTE_ADDR read, same comment). docs/models.md says record_many 'gives each version what record() gives one'; today that is kept true by two copies.
findings.suggested_fix: Extract the address read into one AcceptanceManager method both call (for instance `connecting_address(request)`, returning the address or None), and have record_many raise through the same refusal as record(). No new behaviour; the existing TestRecording and TestRecordMany address and draft tests must pass unmodified.

notes: agreement.js disables the submit button until every required toggle is on, so in a browser running the script a person cannot submit agreement to part of a required list; docs/pages.md 'Agreeing to some of them' describes that path without saying it is only reachable without the script or from a project's own template. Approved on screen (sketch.md:113); recorded, not a finding.
The line under the title says a person will not be able to use the app without agreeing, while FR-024 and docs/pages.md say the page stops nobody. Kept as the maintainer worded it (decisions.md D20).
CHANGELOG.md lists the reserved slug `agree`, which makes an existing document at that slug unreachable, under 'Added'; it reads as a change in behaviour.
views.py module docstring still reads 'The pages that show a document's wording to a visitor', which no longer covers the page that asks.

docs/pages.md says the failure log goes 'to standard error and nowhere else' under Django's default LOGGING; with DEBUG off the default configuration prints nothing for a non-django logger beyond Python's last-resort handler.
